page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high-clock-speed family, powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 33 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and 48 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU), this instance prioritizes core execution frequency over broad RAM density. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark data reflects steady compute capacity alongside robust memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic profiling, the instance registered a strong PassMark memory score of 2,766.23, outperforming general tier medians with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 100.19 GB/sec and write speeds of 52.36 GB/sec. General compute metrics fall squarely within expected ranges for 3rd Gen Intel Xeon processors, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 10,393, software compilation testing at 20,798, and a PassMark CPU score of 25,430.3. Hardware acceleration supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, facilitating moderate throughput for quantized machine learning inference without specialized accelerators.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the ecs.hfc7.6xlarge provides high computational density per gigabyte of memory, making it an efficient allocation for applications bounded strictly by CPU throughput and memory access latency rather than memory volume or disk IOPS. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, which should be factored into total resource planning. Workloads best matched to this instance profile include parallel software compilation, high-frequency continuous integration pipelines, batch CPU data processing, scientific modeling, and dedicated web application tiers.
